ui.heading: Before you begin
ui.lede: This app walks you through running evals on your own AI work. It uses your own AI tool, which runs in an AI window inside this page.
ui.intro: Your AI is your choice. It only needs to be able to read files, write files and run commands. Setup checks everything the app needs, one page at a time, and the steps wait until every check has passed. Depending on its settings, your AI may ask for approval before it acts, or it may act on its own. Any approval requests appear in the AI window, and you answer them there. The app never answers for you and does not hold any keys.
ui.skip_hint: You can skip setup and read every lesson first. Exercises that use your AI stay off until setup is done. You can come back to setup from the reminder at the top of the page or from Settings.
ui.wizard_needed: Finish this check to go on to the next page.
ui.summary_lede: The app checks this computer by itself. Nothing is downloaded or installed, and your AI is not started.
ui.summary_wait: Wait for the checks to end, then press Next.
ui.summary_done: The checks are done. Press Next to go to the first page that needs you.
ui.summary_all_passed: Everything passed. Press Next to see what your AI window looks like.
ui.summary_ai_none: No supported AI was found on this computer yet.
ui.ai_intro: Your AI is the tool you work with in the AI window. Choose one that is installed on this computer, or install one.
ui.ai_installing: The install is running in your AI window. When it ends, the app checks again by itself.
ui.ai_testing: Testing your AI. This runs quietly in the background and takes a moment.
ui.test_signin_note: If your AI asks you to sign in, do it in the AI window first. A passing test also shows that you are signed in.
ui.test_waiting: After you press Send the test line, the app looks for the result by itself. You can also press Check the test result.
ui.project_hint: Your work is saved here. If the folder already has your progress, you will pick up where you left off. Choose a folder outside OneDrive.
ui.project_onedrive_warning: This folder looks like it is inside OneDrive. Choose a folder outside OneDrive so syncing does not interfere with your files.
ui.starter_legend: What do you want to work on?
ui.starter_northwind_hint: A ready-made example. Everything is provided, so there is nothing to bring. It is for practice only.
ui.northwind_note: The Practice task is a ready-made example. It cannot be your submission, and there is no way to submit it as your own work. When you are ready to work on something real, choose My own task.
ui.starter_own_hint: Use the prompt and test cases you provide yourself.
ui.import_heading: Bring your own prompt and test cases
ui.import_intro: Enter the full path of each file you already wrote. The app reads them, checks them, and only then copies them into your project folder.
ui.import_copies: Your original files are not touched. The app only makes copies, and the copies are named prompt-v0.md (your prompt) and test-cases.md (your test cases). You do not need to rename anything yourself.
ui.import_check_first: Press Check my files before you set up your project.
ui.import_stale: You changed a path. Press Check my files again.
ui.import_ready: Your files look ready to import. Nothing has been copied yet.
ui.import_ready_notes: Your files can be imported. Read the notes below first, because they will make your checker stronger. Nothing has been copied yet.
ui.import_blocked: Your files cannot be imported yet. Fix the problems below, then press Check my files again. Nothing has been copied.
ui.test_cases_label: Path to your test cases file
ui.project_blocked: Finish the Choose your AI page first.
ui.project_required: Please fill in the project folder.
ui.own_paths_required: Please fill in the paths to your prompt and test cases files.
ui.term_line_intro: This exact line will be typed into your AI:
ui.term_ready: Sign in here if your AI asks. When it is ready for a message, press Send the test line.
ui.term_sent: Sent. Watch the AI window and answer anything your AI asks. The app looks for the result by itself, or you can press Check the test result.
ui.term_foot: Depending on its settings, your AI may ask for your approval before it reads, writes or runs something, or it may act on its own. Any approval requests appear here in the AI window. Click in the AI window and answer them with your keyboard. The app never answers for you. To move out of the AI window, press F6.

test_only.cli_hint: Test launch only. Enter the command the stand-in AI runs.

ai_window_lesson.title: Your AI window
ai_window_lesson.intro: This is where your AI works for you. Everything you do with your AI in this course happens in this window. You type to it, it reads and writes your files, and it can ask you to approve things before it acts.
ai_window_lesson.alt_generic: No picture is shown for this AI. The list below says what an AI window usually contains.

copilot.alt: The GitHub Copilot CLI window just after it starts. A box at the top names the tool and its version and gives a few tips. Below it is an empty area where the conversation will appear, then a message box and a status line along the bottom.

markers.label: The banner
markers.text: Names your AI and its version, and gives a few tips for getting started.

markers.label: The conversation
markers.text: Your messages and your AI's answers appear here, above the message box. Scroll up to read what came before.

markers.label: The message box
markers.text: Type to your AI here and press Enter to send. When you press a Send button in this app, the app types a ready-made line here for you.

markers.label: The status line
markers.text: Shows the mode your AI is in, such as Manual Approval, which means it asks before it acts, and the model it uses. When your AI asks for approval, read what it wants to do, then answer with your keyboard. Your window may show a different mode.

claude.alt: The Claude Code window just after it starts. A banner at the top names the tool, the model and the folder. Below it is an empty area where the conversation will appear, then a message box and a status line along the bottom.

markers.label: The banner
markers.text: Names your AI, the model it uses and the folder it works in. Your test files and later your project files are in this folder.

markers.label: The conversation
markers.text: Your messages and your AI's answers appear here, above the message box. Scroll up to read what came before.

markers.label: The message box
markers.text: Type to your AI here and press Enter to send. When you press a Send button in this app, the app types a ready-made line here for you.

markers.label: The status line
markers.text: Shows the mode your AI is in (covered here), and which keys change it. When your AI asks for approval, read what it wants to do, then answer with your keyboard. Your window may show a different mode.

devin.alt: The Devin CLI window just after it starts. A banner at the top shows the logo, the name and the version. Below it is a message box, and a status line sits under the message box.

markers.label: The banner
markers.text: Names your AI and its version. A line of this banner is covered here because it showed account details.

markers.label: The conversation
markers.text: Your messages and your AI's answers appear above the message box and push the banner up. Scroll up to read what came before.

markers.label: The message box
markers.text: Type to your AI here and press Enter to send. When you press a Send button in this app, the app types a ready-made line here for you.

markers.label: The status line
markers.text: Shows the mode your AI is in and short hints about commands you can type. Your window may show a different mode. When your AI asks for approval, read what it wants to do, then answer with your keyboard.

markers.label: The conversation
markers.text: Your messages and your AI's answers appear here, newest at the bottom. Scroll up to read what came before.

markers.label: The message box
markers.text: Type to your AI here and press Enter to send. In this course the app sometimes types a ready-made line for you when you press its Send button.

markers.label: Approval requests
markers.text: Before it reads, writes or runs something, your AI may stop and ask. Read what it wants to do, then answer with your keyboard. The app never answers for you.

markers.label: Working notes
markers.text: While it works, your AI shows which files it reads and which commands it runs. You do not need to understand every line.

markers.label: Your AI's status
markers.text: A line near the bottom usually names the AI and what it is doing. If it looks stuck, wait a little, then use the Stop button next to the AI window.

script.label: Script track
script.hint: No technical experience needed. Your AI builds the checker, and there is nothing extra to install.

promptfoo.label: promptfoo track
promptfoo.hint: For technical users. Needs Node.js and about 1 GB of downloads.

track_promptfoo_note: The promptfoo track has the same steps as the Script track, with one extra step where your AI adds your two fixtures to the config. The app runs promptfoo for you.
track_locked_note: You have already finished a step in this project, so its track is fixed. To use the other track, start a new project in a different folder.

working_test.line: Read input.txt, write its contents in uppercase to output.txt, then run python --version and write what it prints to version.txt. Do nothing else.
working_test.headless_line: Reply with the single word OK.

track_script.detail: You chose the Script track. Nothing extra needs to be installed.

track_promptfoo.detail: You chose the promptfoo track. It needs Node.js and promptfoo, which have their own pages next.

python_ok.detail: Python {version} runs the app and is available to your AI.

python_missing.detail: Python could not be run the way your AI would run it.
python_missing.next: Close this window and start eval-coach again, then choose Check everything again.

python_too_old.detail: Your AI would find Python {found}, and this app needs 3.9 or later.
python_too_old.next: Close this window and start eval-coach again so it can set up a suitable Python, then choose Check everything again.

check_error.detail: This check hit an unexpected problem: {error}
check_error.next: Choose Check everything again. If it happens again, close this window and start eval-coach again.

check_timeout.detail: This check did not finish within {seconds} seconds, so it was stopped.
check_timeout.next: Close other busy programs and choose Check everything again.

node_ok.detail: Node.js {version} was found and is new enough.

node_missing.next: Press Install to let the app put a private copy in its own folder, or install Node.js 22.22.0 or later from your company's software portal (Company Portal or Software Center) and choose Check everything again.

node_too_old.detail: Node.js {found} was found, and promptfoo needs 22.22.0 or later.
node_too_old.next: Press Install to let the app put a private copy in its own folder. Your other programs keep their own Node.js.

promptfoo_needs_node.next: Go back to the Node.js page and finish it, then choose Check everything again.

promptfoo_needs_install.next: Press Install to download it. It takes several minutes and about 1 GB of disk.

install_cancelled.detail: The install stopped before it finished.

installed_node.detail: Node.js {version} is installed in the app's private folder.

no_network.detail: The download failed. This computer is probably offline, or the company network or a proxy is blocking the site.
no_network.next: Check your internet connection and try again. If it still fails, install Node.js 22.22.0 or later from your company's software portal (Company Portal or Software Center), then choose Check everything again.

download_timeout.detail: The download took too long and timed out. Nothing was installed.
download_timeout.next: Try again on a faster or more stable connection. If it times out again, install Node.js 22.22.0 or later from your company's software portal (Company Portal or Software Center), then choose Check everything again.

hash_mismatch.detail: The downloaded file failed its safety check: its SHA-256 fingerprint does not match the expected value. The file was deleted and nothing was installed. This check cannot be turned off.
hash_mismatch.next: Try again to download a fresh copy. If it fails again, the network is altering the download. Install Node.js 22.22.0 or later from your company's software portal (Company Portal or Software Center), then choose Check everything again.

not_enough_disk.detail: There is not enough free disk space. This needs about {need}, and this drive has only {free} free. Nothing was installed.
not_enough_disk.next: Free up some space on this drive, then try again.

antivirus_removed.detail: A downloaded file disappeared or would not run right after it was saved. Antivirus or other security software most likely removed or blocked it. Nothing was installed.
antivirus_removed.next: Try again. If it fails again, install Node.js 22.22.0 or later from your company's software portal (Company Portal or Software Center), then choose Check everything again.

npm_error.detail: npm stopped with an error while downloading promptfoo.
npm_error.next: Choose Check everything again. If it keeps failing, go back to the Track page and choose the Script track, or use a different network.

npm_network.detail: npm could not reach the package registry. This computer is probably offline, or a company network or proxy is blocking npm.
npm_network.next: Check your internet connection and choose Check everything again. If it keeps failing, go back to the Track page and choose the Script track, or install promptfoo through your company's software portal (Company Portal or Software Center) if it is offered there.

npm_no_space.detail: npm ran out of disk space while downloading promptfoo.
npm_no_space.next: Free up at least 2 GB on this drive, then press Install again.

npm_timeout.detail: The promptfoo download did not finish within {minutes} minutes, so it was stopped.
npm_timeout.next: Try again on a faster connection, or go back to the Track page and choose the Script track.

cli_enter_command.detail: You have not chosen your AI yet.
cli_enter_command.next: Pick one of the AI tools below, or install one.

cli_not_found.detail: The AI you chose, {command}, could not be found on this computer.
cli_not_found.next: Choose one of the AI tools below, or install one.

cli_not_found_after_install.detail: The install finished, but {command} still could not be found.
cli_not_found_after_install.next: Wait a minute and open this page again. If it is still missing, close this window, start eval-coach again so the new install is visible, and choose your AI again.

cli_chosen.detail: Your AI is chosen and was found on this computer.

cli_start_failed.detail: Your AI could not be started: {error}
cli_start_failed.next: Choose your AI again on the Choose your AI page. If it keeps failing, open the AI in a normal terminal once to make sure it works.

cli_not_signed_in.detail: This app cannot check your sign-in for you. An AI tool that is not signed in usually says so in the AI window and cannot act on files.
cli_not_signed_in.next: If it says you are not signed in, sign in there and run the working test again.

working_test_ready.detail: Your AI is ready for the working test.
working_test_ready.next: Press Start my AI window. Sign in there if your AI asks, then press Send the test line.

working_test_needs_previous.detail: This needs your AI to be chosen first.
working_test_needs_previous.next: Go back and finish the Choose your AI page.

working_test_started.detail: The test folder is ready and your AI window is starting there.
working_test_started.next: Sign in in the AI window if your AI asks. When it is ready for a message, press Send the test line.

working_test_passed_background.detail: Your AI started, is signed in and answered a quiet test.

ai_test_background_needs_you.detail: The quiet test could not finish by itself. You may need to sign in, answer a question in the AI window, or check your internet connection.
ai_test_background_needs_you.next: Press Start my AI window, sign in there if your AI asks, then press Send the test line.

working_test_passed.detail: Your AI is signed in, and it read a file, wrote files and ran a command correctly.

test_missing_output.detail: No output.txt was written, so the app cannot tell whether your AI can write files.
test_missing_output.next: Look at the AI window. If your AI asked for approval, answer it there and press Check the test result. Otherwise press Start my AI window to try again. A chat-only tool cannot pass this test.

test_wrong_output.detail: output.txt was written but it is not the uppercase text from input.txt, so reading and following the file did not work.
test_wrong_output.next: Press Start my AI window to try again and make sure your AI can read files in the folder it starts in.

test_missing_version.detail: output.txt is correct, but version.txt is missing, so running a command did not work.
test_missing_version.next: Your AI must be allowed to run commands. Press Start my AI window to try again, and approve the command in the AI window if your AI asks.

test_bad_version.detail: version.txt was written but does not say Python 3, so the command output was wrong. It contains: {found}
test_bad_version.next: Press Start my AI window to try again. Your AI needs to run python --version itself and save exactly what it prints.

test_incomplete_generic.detail: The working test is not finished yet.
test_incomplete_generic.next: Press Start my AI window, then Send the test line, wait for your AI to finish, and press Check the test result.

project_needs_choice.detail: Choose a folder for your project.
project_needs_choice.next: Fill in the form below and press Set up my project.

project_ok.detail: Your project folder is ready at {path}.

project_onedrive.detail: This project folder is inside OneDrive at {path}. OneDrive can lock files while your AI and the checker use them.
project_onedrive.next: Choose a folder outside OneDrive below. To keep work you already did, move the folder first, then enter its new location.

project_files_missing.detail: The project folder is missing prompt-v0.md or test-cases.md.
project_files_missing.next: Choose Practice task below to get ready-made starter files, or choose My own task and point to your prompt and test cases.

consent.node_body:
The app will install a private copy of Node.js {version} that only eval-coach uses.
From: nodejs.org
Size: about 41 MB to download, about 113 MB once installed.
Where: {path}
Free space on this drive: {free}.
No administrator rights are needed. PATH, the registry and your other programs are not changed.
consent.promptfoo_body:
The app will download promptfoo 0.125.1 from the npm registry into its own private folder.
Size: about 1 GB of disk.
Where: {path}
Free space on this drive: {free}.
It takes several minutes. No administrator rights are needed and nothing is installed globally.

errors.job_busy: Something is already running here. Wait for it to finish.

errors.node_not_needed: Node.js is already working, so there is nothing to install.
errors.track_required: Pick either the Script track or the promptfoo track.
errors.track_locked: You have already finished a step in this project, so its track is fixed. To use the other track, start a new project in a different folder.
errors.bad_install_item: Only Node.js and promptfoo can be installed from here.
errors.type_failed: The line could not be typed into your AI: {error}. Press Start my AI window and try again.
errors.bad_recipe: That install option is not available.
errors.recipe_no_command: This option has no command to run.
errors.project_onedrive_create: Choose a folder outside OneDrive. OneDrive can lock files while your AI and the checker use them.
errors.preflight_incomplete: Finish setup first. Use the reminder at the top of the page, or open Settings, to go there.
errors.corrupt_preflight: The saved check results could not be read, so they will be run again.
